description: Test your knowledge of the knee joint, anterior compartment of the leg, and dorsum of the foot.

cards.text: Which nerve supplies all four muscles of the anterior compartment of the leg, and what is the clinical consequence of its injury?
cards.answer: Deep peroneal (fibular) nerve (L4, L5) innervates tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus, and fibularis tertius. Injury causes foot drop (inability to dorsiflex).

tip.tip: All anterior muscles = all deep peroneal nerve; nerve injury = loss of dorsiflexion

cards.text: What is the continuation of the anterior tibial artery at the ankle, and where is its pulse palpated?
cards.answer: It becomes the dorsalis pedis artery, palpated between the tendons of extensor hallucis longus and extensor digitorum longus on the dorsum of the foot.

tip.tip: Anterior tibial → dorsalis pedis; pulse: between big toe and other toe tendons

cards.text: Describe the key structural differences between the medial and lateral menisci and their relationship to injury patterns.
cards.answer: Medial meniscus is C-shaped, attached to MCL (immobile, commonly torn). Lateral meniscus is O-shaped (complete ring), not attached to LCL (mobile, less commonly torn).

tip.tip: Medial: C-shaped, attached, trapped → often torn; Lateral: O-shaped, free, mobile → escapes injury

cards.text: What are the main functions of the ACL and PCL, and which is stronger?
cards.answer: ACL prevents anterior tibial displacement and hyperextension. PCL prevents posterior tibial displacement and is stronger than the ACL.

tip.tip: ACL = anterior guard; PCL = posterior guard (and stronger)

cards.text: What is the screw-home mechanism of the knee?
cards.answer: At full extension, the longer medial femoral condyle causes the lateral condyle to reach its limit first, forcing internal tibial rotation and locking the knee in extension.

tip.tip: Unequal condyle lengths → asymmetric locking → physiological rotation lock at full extension

cards.text: What is the suprapatellar pouch and why is it clinically significant?
cards.answer: The synovial membrane extends under the quadriceps muscle, forming the largest synovial pouch in the body. Clinically important because joint effusions accumulate here and it can be accessed for arthrocentesis.

tip.tip: Suprapatellar = biggest bursa in body; where fluid builds up; accessible for fluid drainage

cards.text: Which ligament is attached to the medial meniscus, and how does this affect meniscal mobility?
cards.answer: The medial collateral ligament (MCL) is firmly attached to the medial meniscus, restricting its mobility. The lateral collateral ligament (LCL) is not attached to the lateral meniscus, allowing it to escape during rotation.

tip.tip: MCL-meniscus bond = immobilized medial meniscus; LCL-free = mobile lateral meniscus

cards.text: Name all four muscles of the anterior compartment in order (medial to lateral), and what do they all have in common functionally?
cards.answer: Tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, extensor digitorum longus, fibularis tertius (medial to lateral). All produce dorsiflexion of the foot.

tip.tip: All four = all dorsiflexors; mnemonic: 'THE FEET' (Tibialis, Hallucis, Extensors, Fibularis Tertius = FEET)
